title: Session synchronizer: epoch-based lease simplification and prefetch conductor slimdown
creator: Marco Chen
description: Background: Our continuous batching path currently suffers from sporadic latency spikes under mixed short/long session workloads. Root cause analysis points to a hot code path where a global prefetch conductor holds a coarse lease mutex while performing KV priming and session handoffs. This ticket introduces a session synchronizer that (1) replaces the conductor's coarse mutex with an epoch-based lease protocol to allow lock-free handoffs for common fast-paths, (2) compacts the prefetch conductor by splitting priming from coordinating responsibilities, and (3) upgrades a handful of runtime dependencies (tokio -> 1.25, metrics crate -> 0.21) to unlock non-blocking timers and more efficient task parking. Goal: reduce 99th-percentile token latency in continuous batching by 20-30% for mixed workloads, eliminate a class of deadlock racy conditions observed during high admission bursts, and improve operational visibility for lease churn.
acceptance_criteria: e2e benchmark: 99p token generation latency for mixed short/long sessions improves >= 20% compared to baseline (runtime-2026.01) on perf cluster
No regression in throughput at 95p under 200 concurrent active sessions
New lease metrics (lease_epoch, epoch_handoff_duration, handoff_failures) emitted to datadog and visible on runtime-kv dashboard
Migration path validated: old conductor + new synchronizer can run concurrently during canary without observable correctness issues
Automated unit + integration tests covering epoch wrap, stale-lease rejection, and handoff retry logic merged
Security review completed for dependency upgrades (tokio and metrics) and signed off by Security
implementation_notes: Design summary: introduce a lightweight SessionSynchronizer that assigns monotonic epoch tokens per session. Writers (ingress) bump a session epoch when they intend to transition a session's ownership; readers (serve threads) compare observed epoch to cached epoch to decide if they can proceed lock-free or must perform a single-compare-and-swap handoff. The prefetch conductor is split into PrefetchPrimer (IO-bound, runs in a bounded async worker pool) and PrefetchOrchestrator (coordination-only state machine that only touches small epoch metadata). This reduces the critical-section footprint. We will introduce a small in-memory epoch journal (fixed-size ring) for debugging and tracing handoff races. Dependency upgrades: tokio 1.25 for cooperative yields and timer improvements; metrics 0.21 for label cardinality controls. Testing: unit tests for epoch arithmetic, integration with existing kv-shard reconciler, and a synthetic perf harness that mimics mixed short/long sessions. Keep behavior deterministic under testruns by seeding the scheduler deterministically. Rollback plan: feature-flag the synchronizer behind runtime.flags.session_synchronizer; default off for first canary slice. If regressions appear, revert flag to false and rollback tokio change candidate patch. Telemetry: emit lease_epoch, epoch_handoff_latency_ms, handoff_retries, primer_queue_depth, primer_worker_blocked_count. Add trace spans around handoff to correlate with request IDs.

risk: Medium. The epoch approach reduces lock contention but introduces a new class of stale-epoch retries; if not carefully bounded this can create livelock for pathological admission patterns. Dependency upgrades (tokio) could surface await-safety regressions in existing components. To mitigate: incremental canary, conservative retry backoff, and strong test coverage with deterministic scheduler seeds.
